digest.headline: Crude prices breached $93 per barrel following attacks on Saudi energy facilities as global equities slipped.

lede.b: Wall Street shares fell because crude oil prices rose and worried investors about rising consumer prices. Consumer prices are the costs of everyday goods and services. Government bonds, which are like loans from investors to governments that pay a fixed return, saw their yields ease. Yields are the annual return an investor gets on a bond. Central banks, which manage a country's money and interest rates, prepared for upcoming policy decisions. Wall Street stocks slipped as higher oil costs drove these worries.
lede.i: Wall Street equities retreated as elevated crude oil prices stoked inflation concerns ahead of upcoming consumer price index releases. Government bond yields eased across the Eurozone and the United States prior to expected European Central Bank decisions. The Federal Reserve maintained its primary focus on core price metrics despite hot commodity readings. Wall Street stocks slipped on these oil and price pressures.
lede.a: Wall Street equities retreated as elevated crude oil prices stoked inflation concerns ahead of upcoming consumer price index releases. Government bond yields compressed across the Eurozone and the United States prior to expected European Central Bank decisions and domestic price prints. The Federal Reserve maintained its primary focus on core metrics despite hot commodity readings. Wall Street equities slipped as the macro duration trade adjusted to energy-driven cost shocks.

items.i: The DAX index finished virtually unchanged as rising energy costs and contracting exports weighed on sentiment.

thread.b: Energy costs and central bank policies influenced markets around the world. Higher oil prices created worries about consumer prices in multiple countries. Central banks watched these developments closely.
thread.i: Energy costs and central bank expectations drove global market movements. Higher oil prices stoked inflation concerns across multiple regions. Central banks prepared for upcoming policy decisions amidst these pressures.
thread.a: Energy shocks and central bank policy expectations drove cross-asset correlations. Crude oil spikes stoked inflation concerns and compressed sovereign bond yields globally. Central banks calibrated their respective monetary policy stances ahead of incoming macroeconomic data prints.

United States of America.label: United States
United States of America.sub: Oil prices and bond yields move ahead of inflation data

stories.t: Wall Street Slips on Oil Prices and Inflation Focus
stories.b: Wall Street shares slipped lower as oil prices climbed. Rising inflation means prices for everyday goods go up over time. Investors watched these numbers closely ahead of a government consumer price report. Meanwhile, the Federal Reserve, which is the central bank of the United States, kept its main focus on core price pressures. Core measures often leave out volatile items like food and energy.
stories.i: Wall Street equities retreated as elevated crude oil prices stoked inflation concerns ahead of upcoming consumer price index releases. Government bond yields eased across the Eurozone and the United States prior to expected European Central Bank decisions and domestic price prints. The Federal Reserve maintained its primary focus on core inflation metrics despite hot commodity readings.
stories.a: Wall Street indices dipped as high oil quotations amplified inflation anxiety ahead of the consumer price index print. Sovereign debt yields compressed across transatlantic curves alongside easing Eurozone metrics ahead of monetary policy announcements. The Federal Reserve preserved its structural emphasis on core inflation vectors despite robust commodity pass-through.

politics.b: Spain faced a decision about gold deposits held at the US Federal Reserve.
politics.i: Spain confronted a policy dilemma regarding gold reserves deposited at the US Federal Reserve.
politics.a: Spain weighed strategic alternatives concerning sovereign gold reserves held custodially at the US Federal Reserve.

timeline: Wall Street equities slipped as oil prices drove up inflation concerns ahead of consumer price data.
HSBC raised its price target for the S&P 500 index.
Bloom Energy is scheduled to officially join the S&P 500 index.

United Kingdom.label: United Kingdom
United Kingdom.sub: FTSE 100 slips as central bank chief flags price pressures

stories.t: Bank of England Chief Addresses Price Pressures
stories.b: The head of the central bank, which is the main financial institution that sets economic policy for the country, spoke about rising prices. Rising prices mean that money loses value over time, so you can buy less with the same amount. Bailey talked about risks from the Iran conflict. The main stock market index fell following these comments.
stories.i: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey highlighted inflation risks stemming from the Iran war. The FTSE 100 index slipped in response to the warnings. Bailey also pushed back against expectations of an inevitable rate increase.
stories.a: Governor Andrew Bailey flagged upside inflation vulnerabilities driven by the Iran conflict, triggering a pullback in the FTSE 100. The central bank chief simultaneously resisted market pricing for an inevitable rate hike.

stories.t: FTSE 100 Closes Lower Amid Data Deluge
stories.b: The FTSE 100 index tracks the biggest companies listed on the London stock market. This main stock index finished the session down 0.09%. Trading occurred alongside a large volume of economic releases. The market remained relatively quiet despite the heavy data flow.
stories.i: The FTSE 100 index closed 0.09% lower on Tuesday. Trading proceeded amid a heavy deluge of economic data releases. London equities held relatively steady through the session.
stories.a: The FTSE 100 closed down 0.09% following a deluge of macro data releases. UK large-caps held within a narrow band despite external supply shocks and rate uncertainty.

politics.b: Andrew Bailey discussed the Iran war and its impact on the British economy. Governor Bailey warned about rising price pressures. He also pushed back against the idea that a rate rise is certain.
politics.i: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey connected the Iran war directly to domestic economic pressures. Bailey warned about price growth risks while pushing back against inevitable rate hike expectations.
politics.a: Governor Andrew Bailey highlighted geopolitical spillover from the Iran conflict into domestic price stability. The central bank head countered market certainty regarding imminent monetary tightening.

timeline: Andrew Bailey warned on price pressures as the Iran conflict impacted the economy.
The FTSE 100 closed 0.09% lower following economic releases.

Germany.label: Germany
Germany.sub: German shares hold steady as trade and prices move

stories.t: German Equities Tread Water as Energy Costs Rise
stories.b: The main stock market index in Germany, called the DAX, barely moved by the end of the trading day. Shares are slices of ownership in companies. They stayed flat because higher oil prices and climbing inflation made investors cautious. Inflation is the speed at which prices for everyday items go up over time. The DAX index closed down just 0.05%.
stories.i: The DAX index finished the session virtually unchanged as rising energy costs weighed on sentiment. Equities traded in a narrow range while crude oil prices climbed higher. The blue-chip index slipped 0.05% by the closing bell. Treasury and eurozone bond yields also eased ahead of upcoming central bank decisions.
stories.a: The DAX index closed flat down 0.05% as persistent crude oil appreciation exerted downward pressure on risk assets. Sovereign debt yields across the eurozone softened concurrently ahead of the European Central Bank policy meeting. Equity momentum remained constrained by lingering political uncertainty and broader macro crosscurrents.

stories.t: German Exports Contract Unexpectedly in July
stories.b: Goods sent out of Germany to other countries dropped during July. This fall surprised observers who expected trade to grow. Trade volatility caused the unexpected slide in foreign sales. Meanwhile, the overall German trade surplus widened in the latest data release.
stories.i: German outbound shipments contracted unexpectedly during July due to rising trade volatility. The dip in external demand surprised economists tracking export figures. Concurrently, the national trade surplus widened over the same reporting period. Industrial output figures continue to reflect broader cross-border friction.
stories.a: German foreign shipments registered an unexpected contraction in July as escalating trade volatility impaired external demand channels. The merchandise trade surplus nevertheless widened during the period due to a corresponding compression in import volumes. These external sector dynamics underscore persistent headwinds for the domestic industrial base.

politics.b: German political uncertainty weighed on European stock markets alongside rising oil prices.
politics.i: Political uncertainty within Germany added downward pressure to European equities alongside appreciating energy commodities.
politics.a: Domestic political instability served as an additional drag on regional equity valuations, compounding headwinds from rising commodity inputs.

Japan.label: Japan
Japan.sub: Yen surges to seven-month high on rate hike bets

stories.t: Japanese Yen Surges Against the Dollar
stories.b: The Japanese yen is the official currency used in Japan. It just hit a seven-month high against the United States dollar. This means one dollar buys fewer yen than before because the Japanese currency has gained value. Investors are betting that interest rates in Japan will go up. Higher interest rates make a currency more attractive to hold.
stories.i: The Japanese yen reached a seven-month high against the dollar driven by bets on a central bank rate hike. The USD/JPY exchange rate moved to 154.20 yen as the currency crossed the ¥153 threshold. Bullish momentum extended for the currency while the dollar remained firm.
stories.a: The USD/JPY spot rate printed at 154.20 following a break below the ¥153 level. This appreciation reflects shifting carry trade dynamics and mounting expectations of policy tightening. Market participants are now pricing in a higher probability of an imminent rate hike from the central bank.

stories.t: Pay Data and Inflation Pressures Shape Wage Streak
stories.b: Workers in Japan recently received some of the best pay data recorded in decades. However, general price increases, known as inflation, are threatening to ruin a seven-month streak of real wage growth. Real wage growth means pay increases are higher than the cost of living. If prices rise too fast, wages stop growing in real terms.
stories.i: Japan recorded its best pay data in decades, creating a complex backdrop for households. At the same time, rising inflation threatens to snap a seven-month streak of real wage growth. Higher consumer prices erode purchasing power even when nominal wages increase.
stories.a: Recent wage prints reached multi-decade highs, yet persistent inflation risks terminating the current seven-month streak of positive real wage growth. This dynamic complicates the central bank's policy calculus regarding wage-price feedback loops. Real purchasing power erosion could temper domestic consumption forecasts.

politics.b: Global investors are watching how currency changes affect cross-border investments and trade. Major financial institutions like Morgan Stanley and Societe Generale are publishing updates on these market shifts. Companies continue to build business hubs in the region despite the financial market movements.
politics.i: Morgan Stanley stated that currency carry trades can withstand the recent strength in the yen. Meanwhile, Societe Generale noted that bullish momentum for the Japanese currency is extending against the dollar. Separate developments show Samsung opening an artificial intelligence chip research and development hub in Japan for advanced packaging collaboration.
politics.a: Morgan Stanley assessed that prevailing carry trade positions retain sufficient buffer to withstand current yen appreciation. Societe Generale confirmed that bullish structural momentum for the currency remains intact against the dollar. Concurrently, corporate investment continues with Samsung inaugurating an artificial intelligence chip research and development hub focused on advanced packaging collaboration.

timeline: The U.S. Federal Reserve Bank of New York published its August survey showing declined inflation expectations.
The USD/JPY exchange rate stood at 154.20 yen as the currency hit a seven-month high.

China.label: China
China.sub: Exports surge as Beijing injects funds into financial firms

stories.t: China Exports Jump 25% in August
stories.b: Shipments leaving China jumped by 25.0% in August. High-tech goods and artificial intelligence demand drove this surge. Global firms benefited from this sustained import growth.
stories.i: Exports rose by 25.0% in August. High-tech and artificial intelligence demand drove the acceleration. Sustained trade activity supported global firms.
stories.a: August exports accelerated by 25.0%, propelled by structural high-tech and artificial intelligence demand. Sustained trade expansion underscored resilient external absorption capacity for global firms.

stories.t: Beijing Plans Multi-Billion Dollar Capital Injection
stories.b: Beijing will inject more than $50 billion into banks and insurers. The money aims to boost economic growth. Officials released September filings detailing these plans.
stories.i: Beijing will inject more than $50 billion into banks and insurers. The capital infusion aims to stimulate growth. September regulatory filings outlined the measures.
stories.a: State capital injections exceeding $50 billion targeted domestic banks and insurers. September regulatory filings detailed the liquidity deployment aimed at reinforcing structural growth.

stories.t: NIO Capital Fund Secures Supplier Stake
stories.b: An investment fund tied to NIO took a 19.5% stake in a supplier. The deal involved a profit pledge and a founder loan. Haichang faced separate pressures as losses widened.
stories.i: NIO Capital Fund acquired a 19.5% stake in a supplier through a profit pledge and founder loan. Haichang recorded widening losses and rising debt. Xinda Securities cleared a $732 million bond issuance.
stories.a: NIO Capital Fund acquired a 19.5% equity stake in a supplier contingent on a profit pledge and founder loan. Haichang confronted balance sheet distress amid widening losses and swelling debt. Xinda Securities secured clearance for a $732 million bond offering in September filings.

politics.b: Beijing officials announced multi-billion dollar injections into financial institutions. This policy aims to support economic growth. Officials released these financial filings in September.
politics.i: Beijing regulators announced plans to inject over $50 billion into domestic banks and insurers. September filings detailed the state capital deployment. Analysts noted that import cuts helped balance oil markets.
politics.a: Beijing deployed more than $50 billion in state capital toward banks and insurers. September filings outlined the fiscal transmission mechanism. External observers noted that localized import adjustments continued to influence global commodity balances.

India.label: India
India.sub: RBI liquidity actions, consumer surveys, and market losses

stories.t: Central Bank Announces Liquidity Auction and Launches Consumer Surveys
stories.b: The Reserve Bank of India announced a variable rate reverse repo auction to manage cash levels in the banking system. A reverse repo is an auction where the central bank borrows money from commercial banks for a short period. The central bank also launched its regular surveys to measure public views on prices and household confidence. These surveys cover 19 cities to track how citizens feel about their finances. The auction takes place on September 09, 2026.
stories.i: The Reserve Bank of India scheduled a variable rate reverse repo auction for September 09, 2026, targeting ₹5,00,000 crore to manage banking system liquidity. Commercial banks park excess funds with the central bank through this instrument. Concurrently, the institution launched the September 2026 rounds of its urban and rural consumer confidence surveys alongside the inflation expectations survey. These polls gather qualitative and quantitative data across 19 cities to gauge household sentiment on employment, spending, and price levels.
stories.a: The Reserve Bank of India announced a ₹5,00,000 crore overnight variable rate reverse repo auction to absorb short-term systemic liquidity on September 09, 2026. This liquidity management operation runs alongside the simultaneous rollout of the September 2026 urban and rural consumer confidence polls and the inflation expectations survey across 19 cities. These concurrent data collection exercises feed directly into the central bank's domestic demand and price-setting assessments ahead of the next monetary policy committee meeting.

stories.t: Indian Indices Extend Declines as Currency Drops and Oil Costs Rise
stories.b: Indian share markets extended their losses as rising oil prices weighed on investor sentiment. The Nifty index fell to a three-month low. The Indian rupee fell 18 paise to close at 94.74 against the US dollar. Retail options traders faced difficult trading conditions during the closing auction.
stories.i: Indian benchmarks Sensex and Nifty extended losses as rising global oil costs pressured domestic equities. The Nifty index touched a three-month low during the session. The Indian rupee depreciated by 18 paise to settle at 94.74 against the US dollar. Meanwhile, retail options traders encountered volatile execution during the closing auction.
stories.a: Domestic equities extended losses via the Sensex and Nifty as upward momentum in global crude prices weighed on sentiment. The Nifty breached key thresholds to hit a three-month low, while the Indian rupee depreciated 18 paise to close at 94.74 against the US dollar. Retail options participants faced severe intraday dislocations during the closing auction.

politics.b: The state government securities auction results were published by the Reserve Bank of India. States including Andhra Pradesh and Goa issued debt through these auctions. These state borrowings fund local public projects and state budgets. The auction results list the specific tenors and amounts sold for each state.
politics.i: The Reserve Bank of India released full auction results for state government securities held on September 08, 2026. Issuing entities included Andhra Pradesh and Goa, which reopened existing debt lines across various tenors. State-level borrowing operations provide regional fiscal funding while expanding local debt curves. Detailed allotments specify exact re-issue volumes for each participating state.
politics.a: State-level debt issuance proceeded via the Reserve Bank of India auction results published on September 08, 2026. Sub-sovereign borrowers such as Andhra Pradesh and Goa tapped the market through re-issues of existing benchmark maturities ranging from 2035 to 2056. These debt placements dictate regional yield curves and supply local institutional portfolios with duration assets.

timeline: Andhra Pradesh issued its 7.65% SGS due in 2043.
Andhra Pradesh issued its 7.46% SGS due in 2035.

Brazil.label: Brazil
Brazil.sub: Brazilian markets react to polls and oil well approvals

stories.t: Market Rally Follows Poll Shifts
stories.b: Brazil's stock market went up after a holiday. This happened because new polls showed Bolsonaro catching up to Lula in the race. Shares and prices move based on what people think politicians will do with the economy. When a favored candidate gains ground, investors often buy more local assets.
stories.i: The Ibovespa index jumped following a holiday break as fresh polling data circulated. Bolsonaro eroded Lula's lead in the runoff projections, sparking a risk-on move across local assets. Equity valuations adjusted higher as traders priced in the shifting political probability distribution.
stories.a: The Ibovespa surged post-holiday on the back of tightening second-round polling metrics. Bolsonaro's narrowing deficit against Lula triggered a short-covering rally in domestic cyclicals and financials. Market participants repriced fiscal risk premia, assuming a more market-friendly administration if the incumbent momentum holds.

stories.t: Petrobras Secures New Well Approvals
stories.b: Petrobras got official permission to drill three extra wells in the Foz do Amazonas area. Drilling wells helps find more oil under the ocean floor. Companies need government permits before they can start exploring these remote locations.
stories.i: Petrobras received regulatory authorization for three additional wells in the Foz do Amazonas sector. Exploration teams target offshore reserves in this northern basin despite logistical challenges. State approvals allow the energy company to expand its deepwater drilling footprint.
stories.a: Petrobras cleared a major regulatory hurdle with the sanctioning of three supplementary Foz do Amazonas wells. The operational timeline advances regional exploration in the equatorial margin. Capital expenditure allocations will scale as these offshore prospects transition from seismic interpretation to drill-ready status.

politics.b: Election polls show Bolsonaro catching up to Lula in the upcoming runoff vote. Investors watch these numbers closely because the candidates have different economic plans. Political shifts directly affect the value of the local currency and local stocks.
politics.i: Runoff poll numbers show Bolsonaro erasing Lula's previous lead. Foreign exchange desks monitor these political developments closely for currency implications. Election risk remains a primary driver of pressure on the Brazilian Real against the US Dollar.
politics.a: Bolsonaro's narrowing margin over Lula in recent polling has compressed risk premiums in the near term. TD Securities notes that persistent election risks continue to weigh on the BRL against the greenback. Foreign portfolio flows remain sensitive to stochastic shifts in the second-round electoral probability matrix.

timeline: 8 Sep
Petrobras wins approval for three more Foz do Amazonas wells.
8 Sep

Saudi Arabia.label: Saudi Arabia
Saudi Arabia.sub: Attacks on oil sites and falling output

stories.t: Houthi attacks hit Saudi energy facilities
stories.src: circuit.news · The Lufkin Daily News · thenationalnews.com
stories.b: Fighters from the Houthi movement carried out strikes against energy sites run by Saudi Aramco. The explosions wounded dozens of people and caused smoke to rise from an oil depot in Abha. Saudi officials promised to retaliate and stated they will defend the country. Oil prices moved above $93 per barrel following the incidents.
stories.i: Houthi assaults targeted energy facilities operated by Saudi Aramco, injuring dozens of individuals and damaging an oil depot in Abha. Saudi authorities vowed a firm response to the aggression. Crude prices subsequently breached $93 per barrel as security concerns intensified.
stories.a: Houthi strikes targeted critical infrastructure operated by Saudi Aramco, including an oil depot in Abha, causing dozens of injuries and prompting immediate vows of retaliation from Riyadh. Brent benchmarks reacted by surging past $93 per barrel. The attacks inject immediate geopolitical risk premia directly into near-term futures contracts.

stories.t: Saudi oil output drops amid conflict and production agreements
stories.b: Total output from OPEC fell in August as Saudi Arabian exports declined. Conflict disruptions reduced flows from the kingdom during the period. Meanwhile, OPEC and its allies agreed to keep oil output steady for October. Analysts also noted that China's import cuts are helping to balance global oil markets.
stories.i: Total production from OPEC dropped in August driven by a reduction in Saudi exports and local conflict disruptions. Concurrently, OPEC and its allies agreed to maintain steady oil output targets for October. Market analysts observed that demand-side import cuts from China are simultaneously assisting in balancing supplies.
stories.a: OPEC aggregate production figures contracted in August as localized conflict constrained Saudi Arabian export flows. Member states and allies subsequently ratified a resolution to hold production quotas steady through October. Parallel demand-side import reductions from China are acting as a secondary balancing mechanism for global crude balances.

politics.b: Saudi authorities faced direct military attacks on cities and energy infrastructure by Houthi forces. The government vowed to retaliate and defend the country against further aggression.
politics.i: Saudi officials confronted major Houthi military strikes targeting domestic cities and core energy infrastructure. Leadership stated they will not hesitate to defend national territory.
politics.a: Riyadh faced coordinated Houthi kinetic strikes targeting municipal centers and strategic energy nodes. State authorities responded with explicit declarations of imminent self-defense and retaliation.

timeline: 8 Sep
Houthi forces launch attacks on Saudi cities and Aramco energy facilities, injuring dozens.

Nigeria.label: Nigeria
Nigeria.sub: Dangote refinery IPO pricing and foreign reserves growth

stories.t: Dangote Refinery Sets Share Price for Initial Public Offering
stories.b: Dangote priced its upcoming stock market launch at 525 naira per share. An initial public offering, or IPO, is when a private company sells pieces of itself to the public for the first time. Ordinary people and big investment funds can then buy and sell those pieces. The share price determines how much money the firm aims to raise. Trading will begin once the process is complete.
stories.i: Dangote priced its upcoming IPO at 525 naira per share. This initial share value sets the baseline capitalization for the offering. Institutional and retail investors will evaluate the equity valuation against expected refining margins. The pricing mechanism dictates the total capital proceeds the company can secure upon market entry.
stories.a: Dangote established an equity valuation of 525 naira per share for its primary issuance. The offering price implies a specific enterprise value multiple relative to regional downstream refining comparables. Syndicate members will gauge order book depth at this strike price to determine secondary market liquidity post-listing. Any deviation in secondary trading will test the initial pricing assumptions made by bookrunners.

stories.t: Foreign Reserves Exceed Fifty Billion Dollars
stories.b: Nigeria's foreign currency reserves grew past 50 billion dollars. Bagudu announced the milestone for the country. Foreign reserves are pools of foreign money and gold held by a nation's central bank. Governments use these reserves to back their own currency and pay for imports from abroad. A higher total provides a bigger cushion for the economy.
stories.i: Nigeria's foreign reserves climbed past 50 billion dollars according to Bagudu. These external assets provide the central bank with liquidity to defend the currency. Higher reserves alter the country's external balance sheet strength. Import cover improves as the reserve buffer expands.
stories.a: Nigeria's external reserves breached the 50 billion dollar threshold, per Bagudu. This accumulation enhances the central bank's intervention capacity in the foreign exchange market. The expanded liquidity buffer reduces near-term sovereign default risks and lowers external vulnerability metrics. Sustaining this trajectory depends on net oil export receipts and capital account inflows.

politics.b: Government officials reported on economic totals while regional budgets directed funds toward development projects. Local authorities handled infrastructure spending plans for upcoming fiscal periods. Public updates detailed the financial status of different regions.
politics.i: State officials released regional fiscal allocations and economic metrics. Katsina allocated 77 percent of its budget to developmental projects. Regional investment income reports showed disparities across southern territories.
politics.a: Sub-national fiscal data revealed that Katsina earmarked 77 percent of its budget for developmental expenditure. Regional economic performance showed divergence, with Akwa Ibom recording the lowest investment income in the South-South region. These fiscal allocations dictate regional capital formation trends.

timeline: Dangote prices refinery IPO shares at 525 naira.
Bagudu reports foreign reserves climbing above 50 billion dollars.
Katsina dedicates 77 percent of its budget to developmental projects.

Australia.label: Australia
Australia.sub: Australian Dollar strength and Beetaloo Basin drilling

stories.t: Australian Dollar Holds Ground
stories.b: The Australian Dollar held steady against other currencies. This stability came from a strong stance by the central bank, which is the institution that sets national borrowing costs. A weaker US currency also helped support the rate.
stories.i: The Australian Dollar traded firmly following a hawkish stance from the central bank. A softer US currency provided additional support for the exchange rate.
stories.a: The Australian Dollar maintained its footing as monetary policy signals remained hawkish. Downward pressure on the US currency reinforced the pair's resilience.

stories.t: Santos Begins Appraisal Drilling in Beetaloo Basin
stories.b: Santos started drilling new wells to test the ground in the Beetaloo Basin. Companies do this to check if underground resources can be extracted profitably. The site is located in Australia.
stories.i: Santos commenced appraisal drilling operations in the Beetaloo Basin. The activity is designed to evaluate resource commerciality within the domestic project area.
stories.a: Santos initiated appraisal drilling across the Beetaloo Basin tenure. The program targets subsurface data acquisition to determine contingent resource viability.

politics.b: Economic surveys measure what people think about prices and jobs.
politics.i: Consumer confidence surveys track household sentiment regarding employment and price levels.
politics.a: Survey metrics capture forward-looking consumer sentiment across employment and inflation dynamics.

timeline: Santos commenced appraisal drilling in the Beetaloo Basin.
The Australian Dollar held firm amid a hawkish central bank stance.
